explanation: Track the nonzero values already seen in each row, column and square subgrid. Reject an out-of-range value or a repeated value in any of its three groups; zero is an unfilled cell.
timeComplexity: O(n^2) expected time for an n-by-n grid. The bound counts all cells and the actual seen structures, rather than treating Sudoku as fixed 9×9 input.
spaceComplexity: O(n^2) auxiliary space. C#/JavaScript retain sets for every row, column and block; native implementations reuse storage for one group.
attribution: JavaScript port of the independently authored EPI Practice C# algorithm; no upstream reference code copied.
correctness: Each seen set records the nonzero digits already encountered in one row, column or block. Inserting a duplicate detects exactly a repeated value in that group. Checking all cells against all three group types therefore finds every partial-grid conflict without requiring a completed puzzle.
walkthrough: For [[1,0,0,4],[0,4,1,0],[2,0,4,0],[0,3,0,1]], zeros are ignored. Each nonzero entry is unique in its row, column and 2×2 block, so the partial grid is valid. The walkthroughCase uses the judge’s JSON input format and expected observation.
edgeCases: Zeros represent empty cells and may repeat.
Check subgrid conflicts even when all rows and columns are individually conflict-free.
A partially filled grid can be valid without proving that a full completion exists.
